description.narrative:
Detta är ett avtal mellan Sida och FN:s hjälporganisation för Palestinska flyktingar i Mellanöstern (UNRWA), för att möjliggöra humanitära insatser vid de utvalda kriserna: - År 2023: Palestina, Syrien och Libanon - År 2024: Palestina och Libanon - År 2025: TBC
Bidraget från Sida består av finansiering till UNRWA:s två Emergency Appeals (EAs); det ockuperade palestinska territoriet (oPt) EA och Syrien, Libanon och Jordanien, tidigare känd som Syria Regional Crisis (SRC) och UNRWA:s Flash Appeal: 90 dagars initial nödrespons på upptrappningen i Gazaremsan.

This is an agreement between Sida and United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA), to allow for humanitarian response in the selected crises: - In 2023: Palestine, Syria and Lebanon - In 2024: Palestine and Lebanon - In 2025: TBC
The Contribution from Sida consists of funding to UNRWA’s two Emergency Appeals (EAs); the Occupied Palestinian Territory (oPt) EA, and the Syria, Lebanon and Jordan EA, previously known as Syria Regional crisis (SRC) and UNRWA's Flash appeal: 90 day initial emergency response to the escalation in the Gaza strip.

description.narrative:
Assessment covering January 2025 - 22 August 2025.
In 2025, UNRWA is seeking funds to support:
- The distribution of critical food rations for 1.1 million people in Gaza, including nutritional supplies for 1 million people who have sought refuge in and around the Agency's emergency shelters, to avert famine. - UNRWA will provide primary health care to more than 1.6 million people through seven of its 27 health centres that are still operational, including five temporary health centres and 54 mobile medical points. - Inside and around the shelters, NFIs such as mattresses, blankets, kitchen sets and hygiene kits will be delivered to at least 1.2 million IDPs. - Mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) will be provided to IDPs sheltering in and around UNRWA facilities, particularly some 462,000 children. - Protection monitoring will be scaled up through dedicated focal points in each emergency shelter, with identified cases. - As the situation allows, remote formal education will be extended to approximately 300,000 UNRWA students, ensuring continuity of learning and support for their educational needs. - Emergency multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) for up to 100,000 most vulnerable households will also be provided, contingent on prevailing conditions.
In the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, UNRWA is seeking funds to support:
- 275,778 Palestine refugees most impacted by dramatically rising protection violations and access restrictions imposed by the Israeli authorities. In and outside of camps. - With shelter assistance for 15,600 Palestine refugees affected by Israeli home demolitions, displacements and other major impacts on safe tenure due to protection violations. - UNRWA will also repair critical water and sanitation infrastructure in Palestine refugee camps damaged by militarized Israeli operations, to ensure continuity of services for the 230,000 registered Palestine refugees living there. - The Agency will address the basic needs of the most vulnerable Palestine refugees and others affected by movement restrictions, including through food assistance to 136,000 of the most vulnerable. - Access to basic services for populations in hardtoreach communities, including health care for 36,573 individuals and education for 22,500 vulnerable students at Agency schools.
The Agencys emergency planning is fully aligned with the assumptions laid out in the interagency oPt Flash Appeal.
As the largest humanitarian actor in Gaza, UNRWA continues to be affected by the conflict and a lack of humanitarian access. UNRWA reports that their facilities and the people they have housed have been impacted by over 860 incidents since the beginning of the war. The organization estimates that at least 809 people seeking shelter in UNRWA's facilities have been killed during the war, and at least 2,500 people have been injured. 317 of UNRWA's own staff have been killed during the war. The destruction limits the services that the organization can provide. For example, only 7 of UNRWA's 22 health centers are operational. A few examples of the results delivered by UNRWA are presented below.
Food security: During the temporary ceasefire early 2025, it is estimated that UNRWA teams have reached over 2 million people with critical food assistance in Gaza. Since the start of the war in 2023, over 388,000 families (around 1,9 million people) have been reached with two rounds of flour at least 374,000 of those families have received three rounds. In addition to the distribution of UNRWA food parcels, the Agency distributes food parcels on behalf of other UN organisations, reaching over 1.4 million people, since the start of the war.
Health services: According to the Health Cluster, UNRWA remains one of the largest health actors operating in the Gaza Strip, contributing to over half of the people reached with health services since 7 October 2023. UNRWA provides an average of 16,000 consultations daily more than 7.8 million since October 2023. As an example, between May 26 and June 1 2025, approximately 1,120 UNRWA employees conducted over 93,500 health consultations, which represents about half of all primary care provided in Gaza during this period.
Emergency shelter: Between 86120 UNRWA emergency shelters have been managed by UNRWA in Gaza during 2025, providing protection for over 100,000 people. Since the start of the war in 2023, UNRWA has provided more than 1.1 million people with temporary shelter and auxiliary services.
Water, sanitation and hygiene: Daily, UNRWA supplies three million liters of water and collects over 200 tons of waste.
In the West Bank, UNRWA and partners continued the delivery of emergency assistance to the displaced people, in particular in the northern West Bank, including food kits and other in-kind assistance.
Although the proportion of UNRWA's staff who are in active service and the consequences of damages to its facilities are difficult to fully confirm, it is clear that the organization continues to hold a unique position within the humanitarian response. This is particularly true in sectors that are not entirely dependent on the import of humanitarian goods, such as protecting people from attacks and violence, access to basic health care, and water and sanitation services.
Sida assess that UNRWA continues to deliver in Gaza and the West Bank, despite the fact that the organization's capacity, like that of other actors, is affected by the Israeli blockade and humanitarian access restrictions. UNRWA is also specifically impacted by Israeli legislation that prevents them from having international staff and from bringing in goods effectively into Gaza. Despite this, UNRWA remains the organization that provides the most basic social services, and there is no other humanitarian organization that can replace UNRWA in areas such as health and medical care, protection, emergency shelter, water and sanitation solutions, and education. Given the ongoing blockade of the import of supplies into Gaza, these humanitarian activities are even more crucial for immediately alleviating suffering and saving lives.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
